facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Atlasaurus was discovered in 1981 and formally described in 1999 by Monbaron, Russell, and Taquet.
facts.quote: The Atlasaurus holotype was discovered in 1981 and was described by Monbaron, Russell & Taquet in 1999.

facts.statement: Atlasaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian to Callovian stages, in North Africa.
facts.quote: Atlasaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaurs from Middle Jurassic (Bathonian to Callovian stages) beds in North Africa.

facts.statement: The species is known from a nearly complete skeleton including a skull found at Wawmda in Morocco's Azilal Province.
facts.quote: It is known from a nearly complete skeleton with a skull found at Wawmda, in the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian-Callovian) Guettioua Formation in Morocco's Azilal Province.

facts.statement: Atlasaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of 22.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: It has been estimated at 15 m in length, and 22.5 t in weight.

facts.statement: Atlasaurus possessed spoon-shaped teeth that featured denticles.
facts.quote: The teeth are spoon-shaped and have denticles.

facts.statement: The animal had a lower jaw approximately 69 cm long, a neck of 3.86 meters, a humerus of 1.95 meters, and a femur of 2 meters.
facts.quote: The lower jaw of Atlasaurus is about 69 cm long, the neck was about 3.86 m long, the humerus 1.95 m long, and the femur about 2 m long.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Atlas Mountains in Morocco and the animal's large size, estimated at about 15 meters long.
facts.quote: It was named after the location of discovery in the High Atlas range of the Atlas Mountains of Morocco (where the Titan Atlas was said to hold up the heavens), and for the animal's size (about 15 m long).

facts.statement: Recent analyses have suggested that Atlasaurus may be a member of the Turiasauria.
facts.quote: However, more recent analyses have considered it to be a putative member of the Turiasauria.

facts.statement: The most recent analysis of turiasaurs classifies Atlasaurus as a Brachiosaurid.
facts.quote: The most recent analysis of turiasaurs recovers Atlasaurus as a Brachiosaurid

facts.statement: Unlike Brachiosaurus, Atlasaurus had a back estimated at 3.04 meters (assuming 12 dorsal vertebrae), a large skull, a short neck with at least 13 vertebrae of more uniform length, a long tail, and elongated hind limbs.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Brachiosaurus, se estima que su espalda media 3,04 metros suponiendo 12 vértebras dorsales, con un gran cráneo, cuello corto, con al menos 13 vértebras más uniformes en el largo que en el Brachiosaurus, una cola larga y miembros posteriores más alargados

facts.statement: Atlasaurus had teeth shaped like spoons with serrated edges.
facts.quote: Los dientes tenían forma de cuchara con bordes serrados.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest a total length of 17 meters and a weight of 22.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: con un largo total estimado de 17 metros y un peso de 22,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Atlasaurus lived in the middle Jurassic, approximately 165 million years ago during the Callovian stage, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 165 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: Remains were found by Monbaron, Russell, and Taquet in 1999 in the Guettioua Formation of the Atlas Mountains in Azilal Province, Morocco.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados por Monbaron, Russell y Taquet en 1999 en la Formación Tiougguit de los Montes Atlas en la Provincia de Azilal, Marruecos al norte de África.

facts.statement: A second specimen, a near-complete tail, was discovered in Morocco and reassembled in Utah after 300 hours of preparation.
facts.quote: A second specimen of A. imelakei, a near-complete tail, was also discovered in Morocco and was pieced back together in Utah after 300 hours of preparation.

facts.statement: A reconstructed tail specimen was displayed in Mexico City until it was auctioned in January 2018 to fund school rebuilding after the 2017 Puebla earthquake.
facts.quote: It was eventually sent to Mexico and was put on display in the lobby of the BBVA Bancomer tower in Mexico City until it was auctioned off to an anonymous businessman in January 2018 to pay for the rebuilding of schools destroyed during the 2017 Puebla earthquake.

facts.statement: The time range for Atlasaurus is estimated from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)
